keyVerseText: For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth. sift: Heb. cause to move grain: Heb. stone
rootMeaning: The root of כְּבָרָה (kᵉbârâh) is כָּבַר (kâbar), which fundamentally means to weave or plait together, symbolizing the idea of abundance and multiplication through intertwining. This root sense enriches the common English gloss 'sieve' by emphasizing the woven, net-like nature of the implement, highlighting its function as something intricately constructed to separate and sort. Thus, the literal root conveys not just a physical object but an image of careful, purposeful separation and gathering.
usageInScripture: The word כְּבָרָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Amos 9:9, where it is translated as 'sieve.' This singular occurrence underscores its precise meaning as a netted implement used for sifting grain. The consistent translation as 'sieve' reveals the term’s focused usage in agricultural contexts, symbolizing a process of separation and refinement rather than a broad or metaphorical application.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding כְּבָרָה as a sieve rooted in the concept of weaving and abundance enriches our grasp of divine judgment and purification in Scripture. The sieve, as a tool that separates grain from chaff, symbolizes God's sovereign activity in distinguishing His people amidst the nations. This image points to the faithfulness of God in preserving what is precious while allowing judgment to sift out what is unworthy. For the Christian, it reflects the refining work of God’s hand, which, through Christ, purifies the church and ensures that nothing of true value is lost.
keyVerseReflection: In Amos 9:9, God declares His intention to 'sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve.' The word כְּבָרָה here vividly illustrates the divine process of sifting—careful, purposeful, and thorough. It conveys that though Israel will be scattered and tested, God’s sovereign hand ensures that not the smallest grain will fall to the earth unnoticed, symbolizing His preservation and ultimate restoration of His chosen people.
